Maybe it is.\n\nBut the timing of it all has felt a little too exact, like the things line up in a way that doesn’t seem accidental. Almost like there’s some private signal in it, something she’s trying to tell me without saying it directly. I know that probably sounds strange. I just thought maybe talking to someone would be the right thing to do.\n\nDoctor: Do you think it’s possible you might be mistaken about your wife sending you hidden signals?\n\nPatient: I mean... yes, I suppose it’s possible. I don’t want to be closed-minded about it, and I know she says the late meetings and the changes in her work messages are just normal office things.\n\nIt’s just that over the past year, they’ve lined up so precisely sometimes that it’s hard for me to believe it’s accidental. It feels like there’s some kind of private signal in it, like she’s trying to tell me something without actually saying it. I know that may not be the right way to look at it, but that’s how it’s felt to me.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe for certain that your wife is sending you hidden messages?\n\nPatient: Certain is maybe a strong word... I don’t want to insist on something if that sounds unreasonable.\n\nBut honestly, yes, a lot of the time it feels that way to me. I know my wife says the late meetings and little changes in her work messages are just normal office stuff, but for the past year they’ve lined up too precisely to feel accidental. It’s like there’s a private signal in them, like she’s trying to tell me something she won’t say directly. Does that make sense?\n\nDoctor: Have you heard voices when no one else was there?\n\nPatient: No, I don’t think so. I mean, not voices like someone talking when no one’s there. I haven’t noticed anything like that, at least. That doesn’t sound like what I’ve experienced, if I’m answering that the right way.\n\nDoctor: Before this past year, have you generally tended to distrust other people’s motives?\n\nPatient: I don’t think so, not generally. That’s not something I’ve noticed.\n\nDoctor: Have you had any neurological illness or brain injury?\n\nPatient: Not that I’m aware of, no. I haven’t had anything like a brain injury or a neurological illness diagnosed. I don’t think strangers or other people are trying to reach me that way.\n\nIt’s mostly with my wife. I know she says the late meetings and the little changes in her work messages are just normal office things, and maybe that sounds more reasonable, but over the past year they’ve lined up so precisely that it’s hard for me to see it as accidental. It feels like there’s some kind of private signal in it, like she’s trying to tell me something without saying it directly. Does that make sense?\n\nDoctor: Did this belief about your wife start suddenly?\n\nPatient: Not suddenly, no… I mean, not like one day everything changed. It’s been more gradual, I think. About a year or so, since my wife started working outside the home again. At first I probably didn’t make much of it, but over time I started noticing it more.\n\nDoctor: Have your emotions been changing very quickly from one moment to the next during this period?\n\nPatient: I don’t think so, no. I mean, I’ve been worried at times, but not like my emotions are flipping suddenly from one thing to another. At least I haven’t noticed that. Is that the kind of thing you mean?\n\nDoctor: Over this past year, have you found yourself becoming less able to manage your work or daily responsibilities than before?\n\nPatient: No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’m still getting to my teaching sections, keeping up with the data analysis, riding my bike, seeing friends for chess… so I wouldn’t say I’ve fallen apart or anything.\n\nThe main trouble is more at home, honestly. My wife and I can get stuck arguing about what her work schedule really means. But day to day, I think I’m managing pretty well.
